kurz: Why most of the cyclical effect of a government budget arises without any decision being taken, and why the part that is decided works differently from what the headlines suggest.

bloecke.md:
Fiscal policy is made through budget laws that set revenue, expenditure and borrowing. In monetary policy, a committee meets every six weeks and can change an interest rate within minutes. In fiscal policy, by contrast, decisions are taken by a parliament, with readings, committees and a second chamber. From recognising a downturn and adopting a programme to the moment the money reaches its recipients, several quarters usually pass, and in the case of construction investment even years.

This is why the part of fiscal policy that works without any decision deserves particular attention.

## Automatic stabilisers

Rules that are already written into law and counteract a downturn without any new decision are called **automatic stabilisers**. Most of this effect comes through three channels:

- With the **progressive income tax schedule** (Section 32a EStG, Income Tax Act), both the tax liability and the tax rate fall when income falls. Tax revenue therefore falls disproportionately, which supports disposable income.
- In **contribution-financed social insurance**, contributions depend on wages, but benefits do not. Under Section 149 SGB III (Social Code Book III, employment promotion), unemployment benefit I (Arbeitslosengeld I) amounts to 60% of the standardised net pay, or 67% with a child.
- **Short-time work allowance** (Kurzarbeitergeld, Sections 95 et seq. SGB III) pays the same rates on the net pay difference in the event of a significant loss of working hours (Sections 105, 106 SGB III), but preserves the employment relationship. In April 2020, around six million people were on short-time work. A specially adopted (discretionary) programme could not have organised such a volume in the same time.

The advantage of these channels is the timing of their effect, not their size. They work in the quarter in which income collapses. In an upswing, they reverse symmetrically, without anyone having to adopt an unpopular austerity package.

bloecke.titel: Illustrative calculation of the stabilising effect
bloecke.md:
Germany's nominal gross domestic product is around €4,530 billion. Suppose economic output falls 2% below its normal level for cyclical reasons. That is around €91 billion.

For Germany, the European Commission works with a **semi-elasticity** of the government budget of about 0.5. For each percentage point of output gap (the distance from the normal level), the budget balance therefore deteriorates by around half a percentage point of GDP. A gap of two percentage points means a deterioration of one percentage point in the balance. That is around €45 billion, without any law being changed.

By comparison, the federal government's structural borrowing limit of 0.35% of GDP corresponds to just under €16 billion. The automatic effect is therefore almost three times as large as the entire borrowing scope that the federal government can regularly decide on. Estimates of the semi-elasticity vary with the method, but this does not change the order of magnitude.

## The debt brake and the business cycle

The limit under Article 109(3) and Article 115(2) GG (Basic Law) applies to the **structural** deficit, not to the measured one. For this purpose, a cyclical component (Konjunkturkomponente) is stripped out under Section 5 of the Article 115 Act (Artikel-115-Gesetz). In a downturn, the federal government may therefore borrow more, and correspondingly less in an upswing. Deviations are booked to a control account (Kontrollkonto, Section 7 G 115). If they exceed a threshold, they must be reduced in a manner appropriate to the economic cycle.

The debt brake (Schuldenbremse) therefore permits the automatic deficit and only limits the permanent one. It can only be suspended under Article 115(2) sentence 7 GG. To do so, the Bundestag declares an extraordinary emergency and at the same time adopts a repayment plan. This happened in the years 2020 to 2023.

The amendment to the Basic Law in March 2025 added two permanent exceptions and one temporary one. Defence and related security spending above 1% of GDP (currently around €45 billion) no longer counts towards the borrowing limit. The federal states together receive structural leeway of 0.35% of GDP. In addition, Article 143h GG permits a debt-financed special fund (Sondervermögen) of €500 billion, from which investments can be approved within twelve years.

bloecke.unter: Investments from the €500 billion special fund can be approved over a period of twelve years, which works out at around 42 billion a year, or 0.9% of GDP.

bloecke.md: The borrowing of such a special fund does not count for the debt brake, but it does count for European statistics. Under ESA 2010, such funds belong to the general government sector, and their borrowing counts in full towards the Maastricht [[Debt-to-GDP ratio|debt-to-GDP ratio]]. The statement “the debt brake is holding” therefore does not imply that debt remains constant. This conclusion confuses a budget-law metric with a macroeconomic one.

bloecke.md:
## The fiscal multiplier

The **fiscal multiplier** is considered one of the most disputed figures in macroeconomics. It indicates by how many euros GDP rises when the government spends one additional euro. If it is above one, more income is generated than the stimulus costs. If it is below one, government spending partly crowds out private activity.

The empirical evidence is unsatisfactory. In her 2019 survey, Valerie Ramey concludes that the most plausible range for government spending is between 0.6 and 1.0. In 2012, Auerbach and Gorodnichenko found that the value depends on the state of the economy. In their estimates it was well above two in downturns and close to zero in upswings. Using the European consolidation years as an example, Blanchard and Leigh showed in 2013 that the IMF's forecast errors can only be explained if the multipliers were in fact well above one. The forecasts had assumed around 0.5. A single value without stating the conditions is therefore largely arbitrary.

bloecke.md:
## The starting position in 2026

The German inflation rate was 2.9% in August 2026, and 3.2% in the euro area. It was driven by energy prices, which were 10.5% higher than a year earlier in Germany and 14.3% higher in the euro area. The ECB responded on 10 September 2026 with its second rate rise of the year. The deposit facility rate has been 2.50% since 16 September. A government demand stimulus therefore meets a central bank that partly cancels out its effect. This is the typical case of a small multiplier.

In addition, there is the openness of the German economy. Imports of goods alone, at around €1,362 billion a year, correspond to about 30% of economic output. A noticeable part of every additional euro spent therefore flows abroad immediately and supports production there.

There is, however, also a counterargument. The German purchasing managers' index (PMI) for construction was 48.7 in August 2026, below the growth threshold. So there is spare capacity in the construction sector, where the infrastructure money is due to flow. This suggests a stronger effect than the overall picture would imply. Manufacturing reports expansion with a PMI of 54.3, partly thanks to defence orders. Industrial production in July, by contrast, was 1.8% below the previous year according to revised figures. Sentiment and sales are therefore diverging, and the two figures together do not allow a simple answer.

## Distributional effects

Every fiscal measure is also a distributional decision, even when it is presented as a stimulus measure. Three recent German examples show the differences:

- The energy price allowance (Energiepreispauschale) of €300 (2022, Sections 112 et seq. EStG) was paid as a gross amount and was taxable. Recipients with high incomes kept less of it after tax, so the tax schedule made the flat-rate payment progressive.
- The price brakes for gas and electricity (from 2023) capped the price for 80% of the previous year's consumption, at 12 cents per kilowatt hour for natural gas and 40 cents for electricity. The support was thus tied to the volume consumed. A large, poorly insulated house therefore received, in absolute terms, many times the amount that went to a small rented flat.
- The VAT cut of 2020 worked through shop prices. Evaluations showed that it was only partly passed on to consumers. Part of it remained in retailers' margins.

In addition, there is a federal effect that explains political blockages. Under Article 106(3) GG, the federal government and the federal states each receive 42.5% of the revenue from wage tax (Lohnsteuer) and income tax, and the municipalities receive 15%. The other levels of government therefore pay for 57.5% of a tax cut decided by the federal government. This is why such a cut rarely finds a majority in the Bundesrat (the chamber representing the federal states) without compensation.

bloecke.unter: Within five years, a negative yield, at which the government was still being paid to borrow, has turned into a noticeable interest burden. The 2026 value is the September level.

bloecke.md:
## Market reactions to fiscal packages

On the evening of 4 March 2025, the negotiators of the future coalition announced the amendment to the Basic Law. The yield on ten-year Bunds rose the following day, 5 March, by around 30 basis points, from about 2.5% to about 2.8%. This was the largest one-day rise since 1990. The euro appreciated, and the DAX rose, led by construction and defence stocks.

On 23 September 2022, the British government presented a package of tax cuts worth around £45 billion without any offsetting financing. Here too, yields jumped. The pound, however, fell to a record low against the dollar on 26 September. From 28 September, the Bank of England had to make emergency purchases of long-dated government bonds to save pension funds from forced liquidation. In October, the package was largely withdrawn.

bloecke.md: How the market judges a package is shown by the combination of yield and exchange rate, not by its size. If both rise, the market expects higher growth and higher real interest rates. If the yield rises while the currency falls, it sees a financing risk. Packages of the same size can thus be judged in opposite ways.

Regulation (EU) 2024/1263 has restructured the Stability and Growth Pact. Rigid deficit targets have been replaced by a reference path for net expenditure over four years. It can be extended to seven years if reforms and investments are committed to. Two safeguard clauses still contain fixed numerical requirements. With a debt ratio between 60% and 90%, the ratio must fall by an average of 0.5 percentage points a year, and by one point if it is above 90%. In addition, the budget must continue to be adjusted until the structural deficit falls below 1.5% of GDP. The rules are still enforced through the excessive deficit procedure under Article 126 TFEU.

At just over 64%, Germany falls under the 0.5-point rule. At the same time, the special fund arithmetically raises the ratio by around 0.9 percentage points a year. This contradiction has not yet been resolved and is being postponed into the coming years.

First, clarify whether money has only been approved or has already been spent. Between a borrowing authorisation and a construction site lie planning, tendering and capacity lead times. In Germany, the outflow of funds is usually the tighter constraint, not the money itself.

It also matters who receives the money and whether this is already reflected in the price. Construction and defence stocks priced in the constitutional amendment on the first trading day after the announcement, not on the day of the first order.

Finally, it is important to know which positions depend on interest rates. A fiscal stimulus affects long-dated bonds more predictably than equities. A ten-year bond with a duration of around nine loses roughly 2.7% of its market value with a rise of 30 basis points, regardless of whether the programme succeeds economically.

mitnehmen: The tax schedule, social insurance and short-time work allowance make the largest cyclical contribution of the government budget without any new decision: immediately, and amounting to around 1% of GDP for every two percentage points of output gap.
The debt brake limits the structural deficit, not the cyclical one, which is why it is compatible with automatic stabilisers but not with permanent additional spending.
Special funds comply with the debt brake but still raise the Maastricht debt ratio by their full amount.
The fiscal multiplier is not a fixed quantity and depends on capacity utilisation, the central bank's response, the import ratio and the credibility of the financing.
Whether the market sees a package as a growth signal or as a risk shows in the joint sign of yield and exchange rate, not in the size of the announced sum.

begriffe.text: Existing rules in tax and social law that change the budget balance in line with the business cycle without any new decision. They include the progressive tax schedule, contribution-financed social insurance, and unemployment benefit and short-time work allowance. They take effect without delay and reverse symmetrically in an upswing.

Measure of how many euros gross domestic product rises by when the government spends one additional euro. It is not constant and, depending on capacity utilisation, the central bank's response, the import ratio, the type of measure and the credibility of the financing, ranges from close to zero to above two.

Calculated amount under Section 5 of the Article 115 Act (Artikel-115-Gesetz) that is used to strip out the cyclical part of the deficit under the debt brake. It widens permissible borrowing in a downturn and narrows it symmetrically in an upswing.

Measure of how many percentage points of GDP the government balance changes by when the output gap shifts by one percentage point. For Germany, the European Commission works with a value of around 0.5.

Account under Section 7 of the Article 115 Act in which deviations of net borrowing during budget execution from the permissible upper limit are recorded. If the negative balance exceeds a threshold, it must be reduced in a manner appropriate to the economic cycle.
